holidays.name: Kiss a Ginger Day
holidays.description: A day for showing some love to the redheads in your life. You can give a ginger friend a chocolate kiss, a kind note, or a favor they'll appreciate. A real kiss only counts if it's welcome.
holidays.origin: Derek Forgie started it in 2009. He wanted a positive, affectionate answer to the teasing that red-haired kids sometimes get at school.
holidays.funFact: Only about 1–2% of people worldwide have naturally red hair. That makes this one of the most exclusive guest lists of any holiday.

holidays.name: National Marzipan Day
holidays.description: A day for the sweet almond-and-sugar paste that can be sculpted into tiny fruits, vegetables, animals and cake decorations. Bake with it, shape it, or just eat it by the slice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It honors marzipan's long history, and confectioners in Lübeck, Germany have made it since at least the 13th century.
holidays.funFact: Lübeck is still famous for its marzipan. Many bakers there shape it into lifelike miniature fruits and figurines that look almost too good to eat.

holidays.name: National Curried Chicken Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy chicken simmered in a fragrant, spicy curry sauce. Serve it with rice or naan, or try a new regional version.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the world's most widely loved comfort dishes.
holidays.funFact: Curry powder as Westerners know it is mostly a blend created for export. Cooks in South Asia traditionally make each dish with its own spice mix.
